definitions.explanation: The gesture of waving one's hand to call someone closer. In Japan, the beckoning gesture is done with the palm facing down and fingers waving inward, which looks like waving goodbye to Westerners.

examples.japanese: ⟦{店員|てんいん}→店員：00897_tenin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{手招|てまね}き⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{案内|あんない}して→案内する：20203_annaisuru⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: The staff member beckoned me over and showed me to a seat.

examples.japanese: {向|む}こう⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{手招|てまね}き⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えた→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{走|はし}って→走る：00519_hashiru⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I saw my friend beckoning from across the way, so I ran over.

notes:
{手招|てまね}き describes the gesture of waving someone toward you. It is used both as a noun and in the pattern {手招|てまね}き⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧.

CULTURAL NOTE: The Japanese beckoning gesture is made with the palm facing down and fingers curling inward. This differs from the Western palm-up "come here" gesture. The ⟦{招|まね}き{猫|ねこ}→招き猫：06538_manekineko⟧ (beckoning cat) figurine uses this same gesture.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手招|てまね}き⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to beckon (verb-suru usage)
- {手招|てまね}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make a beckoning gesture

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手招|てまね}き⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧: to call someone over with a wave
- {手招|てまね}き⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{応|おう}じる→応じる：02018_oujiru⟧: to respond to someone's beckoning
